a Fe50Mn30Co10Cr10 HEA ingot was first prepared by vacuum induction melting using > 99.8 wt% pure metals under a pressure of 1 × 10 2~1 × 10 3 Pa. The melt was homogenized via 20 min of mechanical stirring under an argon atmosphere and then cast into preheated copper molds.
These blocks were then homogenized at 1200 ℃ for 2 h, followed by water quenching.
the homogenized blocks underwent hot rolling at 900 ℃ with a 50 % thickness reduction (from 20 mm to 10 mm).

The FCC to HCP transformation introduces new phase boundaries and transformation-induced plasticity, synergizing with existing dislocations and twins to sustain high θ ( > 2400 MPa at 25 % strain) and delay necking, thereby enhancing ductility (35.2 % EL).
This contributed 322 MPa to the yield strength, accounting for 40.6 % of the total yield strength (794 MPa).
